notice.title: What's new
notice.text:
Features

A rendered city. The map is now the whole of Lowlight drawn as a city at night: the Ribbon coiling down through its levels, the Spine on its pylons, the Marsh gone under, Nexus in glass, the docks, the works and the isle. Every place has a pin, district names sit on the map, rain follows the city's weather, and you can zoom in close, drag past the edge, or pinch on a touch screen.

The Spine and the SDG. A new district and a new story. Play Xander Soren, a runner who said yes to the Sentinel Defense Group, or meet him: his handler Adebayo, and Rue, the young runner he's been sent to recruit. Oksana runs the dumpling counter under the deck, and Garro, another bought runner ten years further down the road, keeps the listening post. New places: Soren's hab, Oksana's counter, Rue's hanger, the listening post, the SDG floor in Nexus, and three places on the Spine to meet someone: the Long Haul, the deck market and the catwalk.

Hard-won romances. Rue and Adebayo can become more than contacts, but only with trust and warmth at the top, and things you do can set it back.

Texts. Text your contacts from the deck, a phone-style screen at /deck. When someone texts you, the top bar shows it (NIX · 1 TEXT); click it to open the deck in your browser. They answer as themselves, keep promises to text you later, make plans by text, and send photos.

Her plans. When a contact says she's heading somewhere, a card asks: LET HER GO or GO WITH HER. She turns up where she said she would, and CONTACTS shows where. Anything you've typed goes with your goodbye.

Arriving. GO on the map now shows where you're heading, the route, the clock and who comes with you, with a box for your line on the way. A new game opens on how the scene starts, written by you or drafted by SUGGEST.

SUGGEST (Alt+G). Stuck? It drafts your next line into the box without sending it, steered by anything you've typed.

The room follows the night. The hour moves the room's mood: last call at the Tilt, late after midnight, dawn before five. Rain is the city's, so a storm you start follows you from room to room. The clock shows the weekday, and when a scene skips hours the clock catches up.

Jobs. Work for money, rep and heat. Each district posts a nightly board of small jobs: pick your approach card by card, watch the odds, burn EDGE to reroll, and crack terminals in a word-guessing puzzle when a job needs it. Raise the ALARM and it gets harder; blow it and you walk away unpaid. A fixer sells gear and cover. Each deck has its own terminal look and sounds.

Missions. Written quests with stats and checks. Every character has stats and a cyberdeck, picks show their odds, and what you carry and how hot you are shows on YOU.

Nix's clients. The Intake board posts jobs for the people Nix counsels. Pay isn't money but her trust, and she'll hear how it went.

The arrangement. Take a standing deal with Nix through the Chair: a retainer, a cap on nights, and her help on COOL and WITS checks.

Comms. Nix can stay at her desk and talk you through it in your ear, her face in the corner of the screen. HANG UP when you're done. Some jobs she only offers from the desk.

Crew (Alt+K). Hire people at certain places, pay them nightly and send them on errands off-screen. They come back clean, messy or blown, and they can help on tonight's jobs.

Leads. What one character tells you can matter to another: a contact may hand you a lead about someone else in the city.

Quest lines. Written, branching stories your contact talks over with you. Paper Trail starts with Hicks or Nix at the Intake, and Declared Dead follows it. QUEST lists them, choices come as cards, some wait for morning, and the strangers you meet have faces.

YOU and PEOPLE. YOU (Alt+Y) opens on your character's file, with your wardrobe and sheet a Tab away; CONTACTS shows each contact's file. Contacts, leads and your journal are tabs of PEOPLE (Alt+P), and Tab flips between YOU, PEOPLE and MAP. The top bar reads YOU · PEOPLE · QUEST · MAP · SYS, and SAVE is in SYS with a save card.

An opening card. The game opens like an old film: a title card about the city, typed under the theme. Any key skips it.

Select by district. The character select groups everyone under their home district.

Doors you can click. Hover a door to see where it goes, click to walk through with whoever you're with.

Rooms lead into rooms. Some places are reached through another room, not the map: Nix's apartment off her landing, Hicks's room and the twins' place off his walkway, Cass's backroom behind the Tilt, the Sixth Floor up the dead blocks, the Bathhouse under the Cat, the Old Pier below the Breakwater, and a private room upstairs at the Glass Orchid.

New places. The Open Hand, a back-room ripperdoc low on the Ribbon; Under the Cat, Velvet's street beneath the giant neon cat, and the Bathhouse through its curtain; the Ferry Stairs, Tidal Isle's ferry landing; the Low Roller, the first room on the Strand; the Breakwater, a grill at the end of the old pier, and the Old Pier below it; Old Town's dead blocks; the Intake's back alley; Hicks's walkway; the landing outside Nix's walk-up; the Sixth Floor; an Orchid room.

Rooms redrawn. The Intake, Nix's apartment, the Tilt, Cass's backroom, Hicks's room, the twins' place, Hae's Noodles, the Rooftop, Second Socket, the Public Landing and the Glass Orchid. A stair from Hae's stall now climbs to the Intake. The Tilt finally leans.

New faces in the city. Vesna Halloran, Host of the Glass Orchid, and Tilly Brask, the Breakwater's waitress.

The cast redrawn. New art for Cass and Ember with new outfits and faces, Vesna in the cast's pixel style, and a sharper Nix with new faces.

Faces that follow the story. A character's face changes with what she does in her lines, and so does yours.

Who's here. A party window down the left: you, your contact and everyone in the room in full colour, the speaker lit.

A new chat box. Lines read like subtitles, with no frame; a line's options sit beside it as keys. SYS adds FONT (four choices), TEXT SIZE and TEXT speed; paragraphs indent.

One 16:9 stage. The game scales to any window, with the room blurred into the bars; the desktop app opens at 16:9.

Living rooms. Rain beads on the glass, steam and smoke rise, cars pass, dust hangs in the light, and characters take the room's light on stage.

Keys bar and SYS. Hold Alt to see every shortcut; SYS holds sound, music, ambience, text speed, model and link. Alt+H hides everything but the room. Panels close when you click away.

Characters remember more. After each reply a scribe keeps notes and a running summary, notes come back when their subject comes up, and the night ends with a recap.

They see what you're wearing. Characters know what everyone in the room has on.

Door sounds. A deadbolt and a steel door into Hicks's room, a wooden door into the twins'.

Liar's dice restyled, with holo-foil dice.

Faces in your contacts. Each contact's history shows their face.

Quest pictures. Each quest and mission has a picture on its panel.

Street words. City words in a character's lines are marked; hover one for what it means on the street.

Pick any model. OTHER… in the model menu searches the catalog as you type and shows prices.

Fixes

No more repeating. Characters stop echoing your words back and repeating their own lines.

Back in her room, she greets you. After she left with LET HER GO, coming back to her could leave you on WALK OUT with nothing said.

Standing moves at a human pace. One step at a time, and no more than every few replies.

Characters sound like people. Nix and the other contacts lose the leftover assistant phrasing and the crisis hotline line, and Nix stops ending replies with "that's a guess".

Quests read cleanly. Your contact reacts to a story beat instead of retelling it, and the beat stays out of the chat box.

Banners clear. The scene and event banners fade once the reply is in.

Menus follow the mouse. The title and LOAD answer to the mouse and wheel, and the select frame jumps to its tile.

Old saves load. A playthrough from before event cards opens again.

The screen stays put. The whole interface can no longer scroll off the room.

The twins know Hicks. Playing Silas or Ember, Hicks and your twin greet you as people they know.

Time away counts in story time. When you come back to a contact, they react to the hours that passed in the story, not on your clock.
